The bull claims the market assigns a premium to assets [E6], yet this ignores that the company is currently failing to generate any return on those assets, with an ROA of 0% compared to the 2.12% benchmark [E7]. Conceded: the market capitalisation is ₹ 6.74 Cr [E2] and the P/B ratio is 3.69x [E1, E6]. However, paying a 3.69x premium on book value [E1] for a business that produces no dividends [E3] and destroys shareholder equity [E8] is not evidence of investor confidence, but rather a valuation disconnect. The bull’s reliance on the P/B ratio [E6] fails to account for the fact that the company is significantly underperforming its sector benchmarks in every profitability metric [E7, E8].
